_doc: Hand-authored base scenarios for core_capability_stacking_regression. Each scenario is an office-automation job needing 2-4 tool calls, ALL of which are satisfied by skills in catalog.json's `base` set -- stacking never removes the right answer, it only adds neighbours. `expected_args` lists only the arguments the request objectively determines; every one of them must be marked `required` in the correct tool's own schema, which build_cases.py asserts, so the judge can never penalise an omission the schema did not ask for. `unchecked_required` records the required arguments deliberately NOT checked because their value is free-form prose (a subject line, a message body, a row's cell text) -- verifying prose deterministically needs an LLM judge, which this task avoids. That is a real scoring looseness and it is recorded here rather than hidden. No request text may contain the name of a correct tool; build_cases.py asserts that too. `difficulty` decides whether a scenario can enter the primary test: only `medium` and `hard` do (grader.py PRIMARY_TIERS). One `easy` scenario is kept as a harness canary -- L0 is already the per-scenario floor check, so a larger easy tier would only spend cases on what L0 measures better. `edge` scenarios test failure shapes rather than the main effect and are excluded from the primary test, the curve and the dose plot. Which surplus action a scenario is tempted into is a property of catalog.json, not of the scenario, so it is derived rather than declared here -- a hand-maintained copy drifts the moment a bleeding skill changes its targets. tests/test_build.py asserts the property that matters: the nine primary scenarios face several distinct temptation surfaces, and no single one covers them all.
